# Conformance data

What the real core rules give for every goal in every week of the demo workspace. A rebuild proves its rules by reading the same workspace and producing the same rows: every row, every column. `src/spec/conformance.test.ts` recomputes them from `workspace.json` with Faro’s own rules and fails on any difference, so these files always say what the code does.

The ports’ contracts are here too, as cases any build runs through a small shim: [the port contracts](contracts/README.md).

## The input: workspace.json

The demo workspace (Platform Engineering, 126 goals, 5249 check-ins, a 53-week goal year starting 2025-12-22), built for 2026-11-05T12:00:00.000Z (week 45), trimmed to the records the core rules read: the cycle, people, teams, goals, check-ins, decisions (what was said in reviews), asks, reviews and watches, and, under `modules`, the records of the modules that add rows here (metrics). Their fields are in [the data model](../core/data-model.md). It is one JSON object; each array holds one record per line. Asks are under `requests` (the stored table’s name).

## How each week is judged

Weeks 0 to the cycle’s week at `builtFor` (`currentWeek(cycle, builtFor)`: 45 here). Week *w* is judged at its review day, noon UTC: the cycle’s start + 7·*w* + `reviewDay` days, at 12:00 (`weekMoment`). That moment is “today” for every rule. The workspace is taken as it stood then (`asOf`):

- goals added by then (`createdAt`), and not stopped by then (`stoppedAt`);
- check-ins posted by then (`postedAt`);
- decisions made by then (`at`);
- asks raised by then (`createdAt`); one answered or done later is open again with no answer (answered and done are both timed by `answeredAt`), and one withdrawn later (`updatedAt`) is open again.

“By then” means at or before the moment (ISO timestamps compared as text). Days without an update count calendar days (UTC).

**Two cuts, both applied.** Every rule reads only the check-ins posted by the moment. The calculation, the projection and the scorecard (the rules’ “check-ins up to week *w*”) then also keep only those with `week` ≤ *w*; the official status, its latest check-in, the flags and the trend take every check-in posted by the moment, whatever week it is for.

**Not self-explanatory:** goals are taken as they are now in every week: their plan history (`planHistory`) says which plan applied when, but other edits (a stage’s due week, a goal linked to an ask later) are not replayed. The rows are made the same way, so a rebuild that reads workspace.json the same way matches them.

**Not self-explanatory:** two different check-ins are “the latest”: the official status (and `latest_week`, `greener`, days without an update) takes the one posted most recently, by `postedAt`; the calculation, projection and scorecard take the last by week, then posting. They differ when a check-in for an earlier week is posted later (a backfill). Ties (the same `postedAt`, or the same week and `postedAt`) keep the earlier record in `workspace.json`'s order.

Rows go by week, then goals in key order (G-1, G-2 … G-126).

What each column is, and the rule that gives it:

- **status.csv** ([the status](../core/rules/status.md)): `status` is the official status, `goalStatus(goal, cycle, checkIns, moment).status`; `calculated` is what the numbers say (`.calc`, from `assessPosted` in the current week); `greener` whether the latest call is greener than its calculation; `latest_week` the week of the latest check-in (by when it was posted), empty with none; `days_without_update` from `daysWithoutUpdate`. Codes as in [the vocabulary](../core/vocabulary.md). With no check-in posted yet, `greener` is `no` and `latest_week` is empty.
- **flags.csv** ([flags](../core/rules/flags.md)): `flags` the flag codes worst first, separated by spaces (empty with none); `handled` how it is being handled (`action`, `answered`, `noted`, `reviewed`) or empty; `needs_attention` `yes` or `no`; `attention_group` the goal’s group on the Needs attention list (`needs`, `handled`) or empty when it isn’t on it.
- **projection.csv** ([the projection](../core/rules/projection.md)): for a number to move, the projection `assessPosted` makes (to its due week, from the check-ins up to this week), and `forecast_misses`; for a number to keep in range, one number per week (the latest posted in each week), projected to the cycle’s end, made whether or not the goal is stale (the scorecard itself says Can’t say when stale); `forecast_misses` always empty. With no projection every column after `kind` is empty, `forecast_misses` included; with one, a number to move has `forecast_misses` `yes` or `no`. `slope` is the slope the projection leans by (*lean* × the fitted slope), not the fitted slope. `value`, `low`, `high` and `slope` are rounded to 6 decimal places; `first_week` and `last_week` are the weeks of numbers the line used, `to_week` the week projected to.
- **scorecard.csv** ([the scorecard](../core/rules/scorecard.md)): `goalScorecard(goal, cycle, checkIns, week, stale)` with `stale` when the status is `stale`; one row per cell, in order. `cell`, `tone` and `likelihood` are the rule, and all this file holds: a rebuild in other words, or in another language, still scores. `likelihood` is the code (`likely`, `possible`, `unlikely`, `very-unlikely`) on a `hit` cell that has a likelihood, and empty on every other cell and on a `hit` cell that says Can’t say or Too early to say.
- **scorecard-words.csv** (scored when asked, `"also": ["scorecard-words"]`): the same rows, keyed the same way, with the words each cell says: `value`, `label` and `sub` ([every one of them](../core/rules/scorecard.md#the-words)).
- **checkin.csv** ([what a check-in must say](../core/rules/check-in.md)): one row per check-in in `workspace.json` (`checkin` is its `id`), judged again as a draft by `evaluate` in its own `week`, for the goal with the plan of that week (`goalAsOf`), with every check-in in the workspace (the rule uses those for earlier weeks). First the **bare draft**: the check-in’s number (written as the stored number, `String(value)`; empty when null) or its stage updates, and nothing else, the owner’s call left to the calculation: `calculated` (`on`, `risk`, `off` or `done`: `planned` and `none` count as `on`), `reason` (`ahead`, `behind` or empty), `asks_target` and `needs_path` (`yes`/`no`), `missing` (the codes still missing, in order, separated by spaces; empty when it can be posted). Then the same bare draft with only the owner’s call as posted added (`call`, the check-in’s `status`; the posted words, cause, path and target are not attached): `greener` and `call_missing`. Rows go by week, then goal key, then id.

- **find.csv** ([finding things](../core/rules/finding.md)): stage 3’s (`"stage": 3` in `drill.json`), not part of stage 1, where it is scored only when asked (`"also": ["find"]` in `drill.json`, or `--files find`). One row per search in a fixed list (the find rules’ worked examples), made on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (the same `asOf`; people have no job title in workspace.json, so a person is found by name and team only): `kind` (`goal`, `person` or `team`) and `q` the search; `total` how many match; `near` the near miss offered when nothing matched, else empty; `ids` the ids of every row found (the near miss’s when there is one), in the kind’s order, separated by spaces. Goals are the live goals not stopped by then, worst first then by title; people are those not marked as left, those whose name starts with the search first, then A to Z; teams A to Z.

- **goals.csv** ([the query port](../rebuild/ports-at-scale.md#the-query-port-what-screens-and-the-ai-tools-read)): not part of stage 1, scored like find.csv when asked (`"also": ["goals"]`). What the query port’s `goals()` and `counts()` give for each query in a fixed list, on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor`. `query` is the query as a Goals link’s parameters (empty for every goal: worst first, then by title); `total` how many live goals (not stopped) match; `near` the near miss tried when a search found nothing, else empty; then `counts()`: how many of them in each status (`off` to `done`), and `attention` how many need attention under the same query with its attention filter left off (the Goals switch’s count: being handled doesn’t count); `ids` every goal found, in order across all its pages, separated by spaces. `checkedin=no` keeps the goals due this week with no check-in yet, and `checkedin=asked` those checked in by the due day after an ask for an update, by [the habit](../core/rules/habit.md)’s standing (rule 1); `inreview=<id>` keeps the goals that review walks, and none for a review that isn’t there. The contract `goalsContract` (`src/ports/contracts/goals.ts`) runs these rows against any adapter, with its four checks: the rows’ status and flags are those in status.csv and flags.csv for that week; keyset paging gives every goal once while goals are added between pages; no page is larger than 50; only `goal()` gives a goal’s check-ins.

- **navigation.csv** ([navigation](../core/rules/navigation.md)): stage 3’s, scored like find.csv (`"also": ["navigation"]`). For two viewers (`rhea`, who owns goals; `oskar`, who owns none: `owns_goals`) at each address: `menu` the sidebar’s items in order, its groups (your work, look up, make, this workspace and you) separated by ` | `, and `tabs` the phone’s four (More holds the rest), as ids separated by spaces; `owns_goals` is whether they have a goal to check in on (one of theirs, not stopped or done); `lit` the menu item lit there, or empty; `page` the page’s name in the top bar and the browser’s title (rule 2: a goal, review, person or team by its own name from the workspace; Help’s articles aren’t in the workspace, so an article’s page is named “Help”). The addresses with `example` are a module’s item and pages (named “Example”); everywhere else no module adds an item. The last two rows, at the address `/ (Reviews off)`, are Home in a workspace that has switched Reviews off: no `reviews` in the menu, and the tabs without it.

- **import.csv** ([kinds, levels and near misses](../core/rules/import-levels.md)): stage 2’s, with changes.csv, and the spreadsheets stage’s; scored like find.csv (`"also": ["import"]` from another stage). One row per case: a set of rows loaded through the change engine on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (week 45), by `actor` (amara is an admin; tunde is not), into `sheet` (`goals`, `checkIns` or `people`). `rows` is the rows as JSON, column name to cell, numbered from row 2 in order; `answers` the answers given, as JSON, group id to choice (empty for none); `given`, what the case starts from beyond the workspace, as JSON (empty for nothing): `mode` `create` for set-up from nothing (every row new), `stopped`, goals by key stopped before it (in the archive, as a whole-cycle export carries them), and `sheets`, other sheets’ rows loaded in the same file. People in workspace.json have no email, so their email is empty and rows name them by name or ID. Then what the engine says: `kind`, `level` (`must` or `check`), `group` (its group id) and `message` (its sentence) of the first problem or question in the file’s order (sheet, then row; a note is neither), empty when there is none; `must` and `questions` how many Must-fix groups and Check groups; `saves` `yes` when it would save; `kinds`, every kind it raised, notes too, each once, in the order first raised, separated by spaces. Every kind the engine raises has a case ([the issue kinds](../core/import-issues.md)).

- **changes.csv** ([the change engine](../core/rules/change-engine.md)): stage 2’s, with import.csv (`"stage": 2` in `drill.json`). The same cases as import.csv, run the same way, and five more that save (`saves-check-in`, `saves-plan-with-reason`, `saves-new-goal`, `saves-person`, `saves-stop`). Rows are matched by `case` and `row`. Row 0 is the case: `actor`, `sheet`, `rows`, `answers` and `given` as in import.csv; `counts`, every count of the change set that isn’t 0 as `key=n` separated by spaces, in this order: `newGoals`, `goals`, `plans`, `checkIns` (every check-in, those that replace one too), `backfilled` (check-ins for an earlier week), `replaced` (check-ins that replace one already there), `people`, `newPeople`, `teams`, `stopped`, `deleted`, `left`; `unchanged`, the rows that change nothing; `needs_reason`, `yes` when a plan change needs a reason none was given; and `saves`, `yes` when the change set would save. Rows 1 on are its items, in the engine’s order (a sheet’s rows in order, then what they lead to): `sheet` (Goals, Plan, Check-ins or People) and `line` (the row in that sheet, from 2), `target` (the goal’s ID, a new one being `goal_c1` and on in the order the engine asks for IDs; empty for a person or team), `name` (the goal’s, person’s or team’s name), `kind` (`new goal`, `goal`, `plan`, `check-in`, `replaces check-in`, `person`, `new person`, `team`, `stop goal`, `delete goal` or `person left`), `diffs` (every field it changes as `Field: before → after`, the field’s label and values in the words a person reads, `—` for nothing, joined by ` | `), and `needs_reason` (`yes` for a plan change after check-ins started). A case that blocks still lists the items it would make.
- **readback.csv** ([the read-back](../core/rules/read-back.md)): stage 3’s, scored like find.csv (`"also": ["readback"]` from another stage). One row per case: a draft goal (`draft`, the fields set over a blank goal, as JSON) on New goal’s last step, seen by `viewer`, on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (Thursday 5 Nov 2026, week 45, the review day), with the weekly rhythm and Reviews on, each question it raises taken as answered, the level as New goal starts it when the draft doesn’t say (rule 1 of [New goal](../core/rules/new-goal.md)), no metric, and the workspace called “Platform Engineering”. The reviews a goal joins read each review’s `scope` in workspace.json. `rows` is each row as `label: sentence`, separated by ` | `; `after` the “After you publish” lines, separated by ` | `.

- **metrics.csv**: The metric library’s rules ([the library as a place](../modules/metrics/rules.md)), not part of stage 1, scored like find.csv when asked (`"also": ["metrics"]`). Made on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (the same `asOf`), with the metric records under `modules.metrics` in workspace.json (`metrics` and `metricLinks`); a link counts while its goal is live then. Four kinds of row, by `rule`: **find** (rule 1), one per search in a fixed list, `ask` the search as `key=value` joined by `&` (`q`, `unit`, `teamId`, `ownerId`, `dir`, `unused`, `sortout`, `sort`; empty for nothing asked), `total` how many match and `ids` every metric id found in order (every page); **goals** (rule 2), for each metric in use by id, a head row (`row` 0: `total` its goals, `summary` the lowest-and-highest line or empty), then one row per goal in order (`row` 1, 2…): `goal` its key, `status` its code, `slice`, `now`, `target`, `vs_plan` and `owner` in words; **needs** (rule 3), for each metric, `needs` the codes in order separated by spaces, empty for none; **still** (rule 6, [defining a metric well](../modules/metrics/rules.md)), for each metric, `still` its line in words (“Fully defined”, or “Still to say: …”); **parts** (rule 7, [for, which part](../modules/metrics/rules.md)), for each metric, `parts` the parts its links in force use, most used first, each in its most used spelling, separated by “ | ”, empty for none. A **goals** row’s `slice` is the team or “The whole company”, then “ · {part}” when the link is for one part. Every other column is empty.

- **home.csv** ([Home](../core/rules/home.md)): stage 3’s, scored like find.csv (`"also": ["home"]`). For four viewers (`tunde` owns two goals, `rhea` owns goals and is in a review, `amara` owns none and leads reviews, `oskar` only watches) on each of the fourteen days up to the moment the workspace is built for, at noon UTC, with the workspace as it stood then (`asOf`) and `homeFor(homeFacts(…))`: `lead` the lead’s kind (`check-in-late`, `check-in`, `wrap-up`, `review`) and `title` its title, or both empty; `quiet` the quiet sentence and its line, or empty when there is a lead. No check-in draft is kept. Watches carry no date, so they are taken as they are now.

- **zone.csv** ([R3, time zones](../requirements/internal/r3-time-zones.md)): the home zone, scored like find.csv (`"also": ["zone"]`). Its input is `zone` in `workspace.json`, a case of its own: a home zone (`America/New_York`), a goal year starting Monday 19 October 2026, four check-ins (only `postedAt` matters) posted near midnight there and either side of the night the clocks go back (Sunday 1 November, 02:00 back to 01:00), and the moments to judge them at. One row per moment and goal, by moment then goal: `home_time` is the home zone’s clock (`yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm`); `week` is the goal year’s week, counted in the home zone (it turns at midnight on Sunday there, not in UTC); `latest_posted` is the goal’s check-in posted most recently by the moment (empty: none); `days_without_update` counts calendar days between the two in the home zone; `stale` is `yes` at 14 or more. The reference is `src/spec/zones.ts`: read both moments on the home zone’s wall clock and count as the UTC rules do. The rest of the workspace is judged in UTC, as before: a home zone of UTC changes nothing.

Numbers are written with up to 6 decimal places and no trailing zeros; text with commas or quotes is quoted as CSV does. Every yes-or-no column (`greener`, `needs_attention`, `forecast_misses`, `asks_target`, `needs_path`) is written `yes` or `no`; a list of codes (`flags`, `missing`, `call_missing`) is separated by single spaces and empty when there are none.

## How a rebuild proves itself

1. Read `workspace.json`.
2. For each week from 0 to the week it was built for, take the workspace as it stood at that week’s moment (above), and for each goal there, in key order, compute the status, flags, projection and scorecard with the rebuilt rules; and for each check-in in the workspace, what a check-in must say.
3. Write the five files with the same columns and compare them row by row with these. Every difference is a rule that differs: the first few rows that differ, for one goal, usually name it.

A rebuild of the status rules alone can compare `status.csv` first, then the projection, then the flags (which need the trend and asks), then the scorecard.

Regenerate with `npm run spec` after changing a rule or the demo workspace, and commit the files it writes.
